intro: Hello! In this lesson you'll learn the simple present — the tense for habits, routines and facts, like 'I work in an office' or 'She drinks coffee every morning'. The tricky part is the -s for he/she/it, and using do/does for questions and negatives. Warm-up: what do you do every morning?
teachingNotes: Indonesian verbs don't change, so third-person -s is the #1 error (*'She work').
Negatives: don't + base verb (I/you/we/they), doesn't + base verb (he/she/it). Never *'doesn't works'.
Questions: Do/Does + subject + base verb. Short answers: Yes, I do / No, she doesn't.
Spelling: go → goes, watch → watches, study → studies, have → has.
Tie practice to daily routines: get up, have breakfast, go to work, start, finish.
Learners know -s as the plural ending (two cars), so 'she works' feels wrong: -s with ONE person. Say clearly that the verb -s is not plural; it marks he/she/it.
Common transfer error: *'She is work' / *'My mother is drink coffee' (be + verb). am/is/are is only for sentences with no other verb.
do/does here has no meaning of its own (not 'melakukan'); it's a helper that carries not and the question. does = do + -es, like go → goes, so the main verb loses its -s.
have → has is irregular: present it as an exception to remember, not a rule. Time phrases (at six, at night, in the morning, on Mondays) are chunks here; prepositions of time come later.

keyPoints.title: Affirmative and the he/she/it -s
keyPoints.explanation: Use the base verb with I, you, we, they. Add -s or -es with he, she, it: I work → she works, I go → he goes. This -s doesn't mean 'many'. have → has is an exception.

examples.en: My father works in a bank.

id.title: Kalimat positif dan -s untuk he/she/it
id.explanation: Pakai kata kerja bentuk dasar dengan I, you, we, they. Tambahkan -s atau -es dengan he, she, it: I work → she works, I go → he goes. -s ini tidak berarti 'banyak'. have → has adalah pengecualian.

keyPoints.title: Negatives with don't / doesn't
keyPoints.explanation: don't + base verb for I/you/we/they; doesn't + base verb for he/she/it. do/does is only a helper (it doesn't mean 'melakukan' here). The -s moves to 'does', so the main verb has no -s.

id.title: Kalimat negatif dengan don't / doesn't
id.explanation: don't + kata kerja dasar untuk I/you/we/they; doesn't + kata kerja dasar untuk he/she/it. do/does di sini hanya kata bantu (tidak berarti 'melakukan'). -s pindah ke 'does', jadi kata kerja utamanya tidak memakai -s.

keyPoints.title: Questions with do / does
keyPoints.explanation: Do/Does + subject + base verb: Do you play football? Does he live here? Do/Does at the start works like 'apakah'. Answer with do/does, not the main verb: Yes, I do. / No, he doesn't.

examples.en: Do you speak English? — Yes, I do.
examples.id: Apakah kamu bisa berbahasa Inggris? — Ya.

examples.en: What time does she start work?

id.title: Pertanyaan dengan do / does
id.explanation: Do/Does + subjek + kata kerja dasar: Do you play football? Does he live here? Do/Does di awal kalimat berfungsi seperti 'apakah'. Jawab dengan do/does, bukan dengan kata kerja utamanya: Yes, I do. / No, he doesn't.

assessment.rubric: Any correct simple present sentence about an evening routine scores 100. Third-person or tense errors reduce the score.

blocks.text: Use the simple present for **habits**, **routines** and **facts**: things that are generally true, not just right now. A **tense** is the form of a verb that shows time. Indonesian verbs never change; you add words like *biasanya* or *setiap hari*. English also changes the verb a little. Time words like *every day*, *usually* and *on Mondays* are a good sign.

id.text: Simple present dipakai untuk **kebiasaan**, **rutinitas** dan **fakta**: hal yang umumnya benar, bukan hanya saat ini. **Tense** adalah bentuk kata kerja yang menunjukkan waktu. Kata kerja bahasa Indonesia tidak pernah berubah; kamu cukup menambah kata seperti *biasanya* atau *setiap hari*. Bahasa Inggris juga sedikit mengubah kata kerjanya. Kata waktu seperti *every day*, *usually* dan *on Mondays* adalah tandanya.

rows.en: We go to the gym on Mondays.

blocks.text:
With I, you, we and they, use the **base verb**: the plain dictionary form (*work, go, study*). With **he, she, it** (one person or thing: *my father, Rina, the app*) add **-s**: *she works*.

This surprises many learners: you know **-s** as 'many' (*two cars*). On a verb it means something else: it marks **one** person or thing (he, she, it). Same letter, different job.

Spelling: add **-es** after s, sh, ch, x and o: *he watches, she goes*. A consonant + y becomes **-ies**: *study → studies*. And **have** becomes **has**. The next section shows why.

id.text:
Dengan I, you, we dan they, pakai **kata kerja dasar**: bentuk polos seperti di kamus (*work, go, study*). Dengan **he, she, it** (satu orang atau benda: *my father, Rina, the app*) tambahkan **-s**: *she works*.

Ini sering membingungkan: kamu tahu **-s** sebagai tanda 'banyak' (*two cars*). Di kata kerja, artinya lain: -s justru menandai **satu** orang atau benda (he, she, it). Hurufnya sama, tugasnya beda.

Ejaan: tambahkan **-es** setelah s, sh, ch, x dan o: *he watches, she goes*. Huruf mati + y menjadi **-ies**: *study → studies*. Dan **have** menjadi **has**. Bagian berikutnya menjelaskan alasannya.

rows.en: My father works in a bank.
She goes to school by bus.

blocks.explain: Watch ends in ch. 'watchs' is hard to say, so we add -es and an extra 'iz' sound: watches.

id.explain: Watch berakhiran ch. 'watchs' susah diucapkan, jadi ditambah -es dan bunyi 'iz': watches.
id.prompt: Lengkapi: My sister ___ TV every evening.

blocks.text:
Most verbs just add **-s**. A few change their spelling, and there's a reason:
- After **s, sh, ch, x**, a plain -s is hard to say, so we add **-es** and you hear an extra 'iz' sound: *watch → watches* ('wot-chiz').
- After **o**, add **-es**: *go → goes*, *do → does*.
- After a **consonant + y**, the y changes to **i** and you add **-es**: *study → studies*. After a **vowel + y**, just add -s: *play → plays*.
- **have → has** follows no rule. It's an exception: just remember it. 'He haves' is always wrong.

**Vowels** are the letters a, e, i, o, u (huruf hidup); **consonants** are all the other letters (huruf mati).

id.text:
Kebanyakan kata kerja cukup ditambah **-s**. Beberapa berubah ejaannya, dan ada alasannya:
- Setelah **s, sh, ch, x**, -s saja susah diucapkan, jadi ditambah **-es** dan terdengar bunyi tambahan 'iz': *watch → watches* ('wot-chiz').
- Setelah **o**, tambahkan **-es**: *go → goes*, *do → does*.
- Setelah **huruf mati + y**, y berubah jadi **i** lalu ditambah **-es**: *study → studies*. Setelah **huruf hidup + y**, cukup tambah -s: *play → plays*.
- **have → has** tidak ikut aturan apa pun. Ini pengecualian: hafalkan saja. 'He haves' selalu salah.

**Huruf hidup (vokal)** adalah a, e, i, o, u; **huruf mati (konsonan)** adalah semua huruf lainnya.

blocks.text: You'll also see -s on nouns: *two cars*, *on Mondays* (= every Monday). That's the 'many' -s. In *she works* the -s is on the verb and means one person. Don't mix them up.

id.text: Kamu juga akan melihat -s di kata benda: *two cars*, *on Mondays* (= setiap hari Senin). Itu -s untuk 'banyak'. Di *she works*, -s ada di kata kerja dan artinya satu orang. Jangan tertukar.

blocks.explain: Budi = he, so add -s. Play ends in a vowel + y (a + y), so just add -s: plays.

id.explain: Budi = he, jadi tambahkan -s. Play berakhiran huruf hidup + y (a + y), jadi cukup tambah -s: plays.

blocks.text: Use **don't** + base verb with I/you/we/they and **doesn't** + base verb with he/she/it. Here **do/does** is only a helper word: it doesn't mean 'melakukan', it just carries *not*. **does** is *do* + -es (like *go → goes*), so it already has the -s. That's why the action word has **no -s**: *She doesn't like rain*, not 'doesn't likes'.

id.text: Pakai **don't** + kata kerja dasar untuk I/you/we/they dan **doesn't** + kata kerja dasar untuk he/she/it. Di sini **do/does** hanya kata bantu: artinya bukan 'melakukan', ia cuma membawa *not*. **does** adalah *do* + -es (seperti *go → goes*), jadi -s-nya sudah ada di situ. Karena itu kata kegiatannya **tanpa -s**: *She doesn't like rain*, bukan 'doesn't likes'.

blocks.explain: He → doesn't, and the verb stays in the base form: eat.

id.explain: He → doesn't, dan kata kerjanya tetap bentuk dasar: eat.

blocks.text: Start with **Do** or **Does**, then the subject, then the base verb: *Do you speak English? Does he live here?* **Do/Does** at the start works like **apakah**. Short answers repeat do/does, not the action word: **Yes, I do. / No, he doesn't.** (not 'Yes, I speak').

id.text: Mulai dengan **Do** atau **Does**, lalu subjek, lalu kata kerja dasar: *Do you speak English? Does he live here?* **Do/Does** di awal kalimat fungsinya seperti **apakah**. Jawaban singkat mengulang do/does, bukan kata kegiatannya: **Yes, I do. / No, he doesn't.** (bukan 'Yes, I speak').

rows.en: Do you speak English? — Yes, I do.
rows.id: Apakah kamu bisa berbahasa Inggris? — Ya.

rows.en: What time does she start work?

blocks.explain: Your brother is one person (= he), so Does. Is is wrong because play is a normal verb: am/is/are is only for sentences with no other verb.

id.explain: Your brother itu satu orang (= he), jadi Does. Is salah karena play adalah kata kerja biasa: am/is/are hanya untuk kalimat tanpa kata kerja lain.

blocks.text: Talking about your routine is one of the first real conversations you'll have: *I start work at nine. I usually have lunch at twelve. In the evening I cook and watch TV.* It's also the tense of instructions and documentation: *The app saves your work automatically.*

id.text: Menceritakan rutinitas adalah salah satu percakapan nyata pertama yang akan kamu alami: *I start work at nine. I usually have lunch at twelve. In the evening I cook and watch TV.* Ini juga tense untuk instruksi dan dokumentasi: *The app saves your work automatically.*

blocks.text: Most mistakes are the missing -s with he/she/it. Check every he/she/it sentence once.

id.text: Kesalahan paling sering adalah lupa -s untuk he/she/it. Periksa setiap kalimat he/she/it sekali lagi.

blocks.text: The small words before times are fixed: **at** + a clock time (*at six*) or *at night*, **in the** morning / afternoon / evening, **on** + a day (*on Mondays*). For now, learn them as ready-made chunks.

id.text: Kata kecil sebelum waktu itu sudah tetap: **at** + jam (*at six*) atau *at night*, **in the** morning / afternoon / evening, **on** + hari (*on Mondays*). Untuk sekarang, hafalkan saja sebagai satu paket.

suggestedQuestions: Why do we add -s with he/she/it?
Why is it 'doesn't like', not 'doesn't likes'?
How is this different from am/is/are?

id.intro: Halo! Di pelajaran ini kamu akan belajar simple present — tense untuk kebiasaan, rutinitas dan fakta, seperti 'I work in an office' atau 'She drinks coffee every morning'. Bagian yang menantang adalah tambahan -s untuk he/she/it, serta do/does untuk pertanyaan dan kalimat negatif. Pemanasan: apa yang kamu lakukan setiap pagi?
